newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chesterfield takes stake in flour mill.
newsitem.headline: Chesterfield takes stake in flour mill.

text.p: Property investment and food manufacturing concern Chesterfield Ltd said on Tuesday it would buy a stake in a flour mill joint venture in China from third party Luck Patron Profits Ltd for HK$52 million.
In a statement, Chesterfield said it has agreed to buy Seabright Holdings Ltd, a company holding a 60 percent interest in Sino-foreign joint venture Nanjing Youheng Wheatflour Co Ltd.
The remaining 40 percent of Nanjing Youheng Wheatflour is held by Chinese state company Nanjing Flour Mill.
Nanjing Youheng Wheatflour, with paid-up capital of HK$52.6 million, manufactures and trades flour products in China.
Chesterfield said no government approval was required in China for the acquisition.
The company said it would fund the purchase by internal resources -- HK$30 million in cash, with the balance either paid in cash or raised through the issue of new shares.
Chesterfield now operates flour mills in Lianyungang in Jiangsu province and in Dingyuan in Anhui province.
"The acquisition will increase the maximum capacity of flour production from the existing 90,000 tons per annum to 290,000 tons per annum," the statement said.
Chesterfield shares were unchanged at HK$0.209 in late morning.
